auto: As a variable type, the type is deduced automatically from its initializer (`auto d = 5.0;` is a double; `auto a;` is an error). As a function return type, deduced from the return statements; the instructor discourages that use. See [auto and the ranged for](#/comp3522-w6/auto-ranged-for).
trailing return type: `auto add(int x, int y) -> int;`: here `auto` does no type inference; it is syntax that moves the return type after the parameters so declarations line up. See [auto and the ranged for](#/comp3522-w6/auto-ranged-for).
ranged for|for-each loop: `for (const int& i : v)`: a for loop over a specified range, identical to Java's for-each; the initializer may be a container, a braced-init-list or an array. See [auto and the ranged for](#/comp3522-w6/auto-ranged-for).
STL|Standard Template Library: C++'s "Java Collections Framework SUPERPOWERED": containers (classes that store objects), iterators (for working on a sequence of values) and algorithms (functions designed for a range of elements). See [The STL: containers, iterators, algorithms, and the vector again](#/comp3522-w6/stl-overview-vector).
value semantics: Containers get a copy of the object put in them, so an element class needs a copy constructor, an assignment operator and a destructor. See [The STL: containers, iterators, algorithms, and the vector again](#/comp3522-w6/stl-overview-vector).
half-open range|[first, last): The STL convention: the first position is included, the last excluded; array[0,5) covers indexes 0 to 4. See [The STL: containers, iterators, algorithms, and the vector again](#/comp3522-w6/stl-overview-vector).
sequence container: A container whose order we specify: array, vector, deque, list, forward_list. See [The STL: containers, iterators, algorithms, and the vector again](#/comp3522-w6/stl-overview-vector).
associative container: A container that sorts its objects automatically and searches in O(log n): set, multiset, map, multimap. See [The STL: containers, iterators, algorithms, and the vector again](#/comp3522-w6/stl-overview-vector).
unordered associative container: A container that stores by hash and searches in O(1) to O(n) worst case: unordered_set, unordered_multiset, unordered_map, unordered_multimap. See [The STL: containers, iterators, algorithms, and the vector again](#/comp3522-w6/stl-overview-vector).
first-class container: vector, list, deque, map and multimap, set and multiset. See [First-class containers and adaptors, pair, map and multimap](#/comp3522-w6/containers-pair-map).
container adaptor: A class that modifies and restricts a first-class container: stack and queue (default implementation the deque), priority_queue (default implementation the vector). See [First-class containers and adaptors, pair, map and multimap](#/comp3522-w6/containers-pair-map).
pair: An object from `<utility>` that holds two values of different types, with accessors `first` and `second`; `make_pair` builds one. See [First-class containers and adaptors, pair, map and multimap](#/comp3522-w6/containers-pair-map).
map: A sorted associative container of 1-to-1 key/value pairs; `value_type` is a pair; keys must be unique and are sorted by a comparison function; logarithmic search, insertion and removal. See [First-class containers and adaptors, pair, map and multimap](#/comp3522-w6/containers-pair-map).
value_type: The element type of a container; for a map, the pair that combines key and value. See [First-class containers and adaptors, pair, map and multimap](#/comp3522-w6/containers-pair-map).
multimap: A map that allows duplicate keys; equal keys are found with `find` and `count` or with `equal_range`. See [First-class containers and adaptors, pair, map and multimap](#/comp3522-w6/containers-pair-map).
deque: A double-ended queue: `push_front`, `push_back`, `pop_front`, `pop_back`, `at`, `front`, `back`. See [First-class containers and adaptors, pair, map and multimap](#/comp3522-w6/containers-pair-map).
priority_queue: An adaptor (on a vector) whose `top()` is the largest element by `operator<`; `push` and `pop`. See [First-class containers and adaptors, pair, map and multimap](#/comp3522-w6/containers-pair-map).
set: An associative container of sorted unique objects; the value identifies the element; elements are const once inserted; typically a binary search tree; logarithmic operations. See [set, multiset and strict weak ordering](#/comp3522-w6/set-strict-weak-ordering).
multiset: A set that keeps duplicates; `erase(key)` removes every equal element. See [set, multiset and strict weak ordering](#/comp3522-w6/set-strict-weak-ordering).
Compare concept|compare: A type satisfies Compare if it is a binary predicate (returns true or false) and induces a strict weak ordering. See [set, multiset and strict weak ordering](#/comp3522-w6/set-strict-weak-ordering).
strict weak ordering: A comparison lessThan is a strict weak ordering iff it is irreflexive (lessThan(x, x) is false), antisymmetric (lessThan(x, y) implies !lessThan(y, x)) and transitive (lessThan(x, y) and lessThan(y, z) imply lessThan(x, z)). See [set, multiset and strict weak ordering](#/comp3522-w6/set-strict-weak-ordering).
binary predicate: A function that takes two elements and returns a boolean; one of the three ways to define an ordering. See [set, multiset and strict weak ordering](#/comp3522-w6/set-strict-weak-ordering).
functor: An object that behaves like a function: a struct with `operator()`; the third way to define a comparison. See [set, multiset and strict weak ordering](#/comp3522-w6/set-strict-weak-ordering).
typedef: Creates an alias usable anywhere instead of a (possibly complex) type name: `typedef int int_t;`, `typedef int arr_t[3];`, `typedef map<string, string>::iterator mapIterator;`. See [typedefs: the restaurant analogy and the standard container typedefs](#/comp3522-w6/typedefs-restaurant).
restaurant analogy: Every restaurant typedefs its own menu type as `menu`, so "Can I get a menu?" works everywhere; every STL container typedefs its own iterator type as `iterator`, so `vector<int>::iterator` and `map<string, int>::iterator` both work. See [typedefs: the restaurant analogy and the standard container typedefs](#/comp3522-w6/typedefs-restaurant).
standard container typedefs: size_type, value_type, iterator, pointer, reference and const_reference, difference_type; they make generic functions on containers possible. See [typedefs: the restaurant analogy and the standard container typedefs](#/comp3522-w6/typedefs-restaurant).
size_type: An unsigned integer type large enough to hold the size of any object of that class; in all first-class containers and adaptors. See [typedefs: the restaurant analogy and the standard container typedefs](#/comp3522-w6/typedefs-restaurant).
const_iterator: An iterator that prevents modification of the elements during iteration. See [typedefs: the restaurant analogy and the standard container typedefs](#/comp3522-w6/typedefs-restaurant).
reverse_iterator: Iterates backwards starting from the last element with `rbegin()`; incrementing moves toward the beginning. See [typedefs: the restaurant analogy and the standard container typedefs](#/comp3522-w6/typedefs-restaurant).
iterator: An object that points to some element in a range and can iterate through the range with operators like `++` and `*`; used to iterate generically and to call STL algorithms. See [Iterators: begin, end and one past the last](#/comp3522-w6/begin-end).
begin(): Returns an iterator to the first element of the container, if it exists. See [Iterators: begin, end and one past the last](#/comp3522-w6/begin-end).
end(): Returns an iterator to a theoretical one element past the last; it does not point to an element and must not be dereferenced. See [Iterators: begin, end and one past the last](#/comp3522-w6/begin-end).
input iterator: Single pass, forward, read only: `==`, `!=`, `++`, `*it`. See [The five kinds of iterator](#/comp3522-w6/iterator-kinds).
output iterator: Single pass, forward, write only: `*it = value`, `++`. See [The five kinds of iterator](#/comp3522-w6/iterator-kinds).
forward iterator: Multi-pass, forward, read and write; a copy can be kept and dereferenced later. See [The five kinds of iterator](#/comp3522-w6/iterator-kinds).
bidirectional iterator: A forward iterator that also supports `--`; the iterator of list, set, map. See [The five kinds of iterator](#/comp3522-w6/iterator-kinds).
random access iterator: A bidirectional iterator that also supports `it + n`, `it - n`, `+=`, `-=`, `it1 - it2` (difference_type), `it[n]` and `<`; the iterator of vector and deque. See [The five kinds of iterator](#/comp3522-w6/iterator-kinds).
difference_type: The signed type returned by subtracting one random access iterator from another. See [The five kinds of iterator](#/comp3522-w6/iterator-kinds).
STL algorithm|algorithm: A function used on a range [first, last) of an array or container through iterators or pointers; it does not change the size of the container; most live in `<algorithm>`, a few in `<numeric>`. See [STL algorithms and std::partition](#/comp3522-w6/algorithms-partition).
predicate|unary predicate: A function that accepts one element and returns a boolean, passed to algorithms such as partition. See [STL algorithms and std::partition](#/comp3522-w6/algorithms-partition).
partition|std: :partition: Reorders [first, last) so every element for which the predicate is true precedes every element for which it is false; relative order is not maintained; returns an iterator to the first element of the false group, or end if that group is empty. See [STL algorithms and std::partition](#/comp3522-w6/algorithms-partition).
iter_swap: Swaps the elements two iterators point at; the move inside partition's implementation. See [STL algorithms and std::partition](#/comp3522-w6/algorithms-partition).
find_if_not: Returns the first iterator in the range whose element makes the predicate false. See [STL algorithms and std::partition](#/comp3522-w6/algorithms-partition).
for_each: Applies a function to every element of a range: `for_each(cities.begin(), cities.end(), print)`. See [The three activities, worked](#/comp3522-w6/activities-worked).
